headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty snapped two-week gains as surging crude oil prices triggered a volatile weekly decline.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 26 October.

why: Brent crude oil prices surged above $117 following Houthi-Saudi attacks, impacting energy-sensitive markets
Geopolitical tensions and volatility in global bond markets weighed heavily on investor sentiment
Profit booking after two weeks of gains led to a sharp intraday crash from the day's highs
Concerns over rising energy costs and potential inflation dampened domestic equity performance
whatHappening: The Nifty 50 ended the week at 22,600 while the Sensex shed 1,600 points during a turbulent trading week
BPCL reported a significant turnaround, swinging to a profit of Rs 4,993 crore in its Q2 results
SEBI imposed a Rs 11.5 crore penalty and ordered a refund against Avadhut Sathe Trading Academy
IT stocks saw renewed buying interest after a three-day fall, with Infosys declaring an interim dividend
summary: On the last trading day, Indian markets ended a turbulent week in the red as Brent crude oil prices spiked to six-month highs. Despite a mid-session rebound led by IT stocks and positive Q2 results from BPCL, the Sensex and Nifty closed lower. Investors remained cautious due to geopolitical risks and regulatory actions by SEBI.
